subject.title: Add Atomic Chat as a bundled local provider (OpenAI-compatible, 127.0.0.1:1337)

question: Should Atomic Chat be promoted into OpenClaw as a bundled enabled-by-default provider, or should it remain external/custom-provider documentation?
rationale: Current OpenClaw already supports custom OpenAI-compatible providers and external provider plugins, while bundling Atomic Chat would expand first-party provider/auth/onboarding surface.

options.title: Keep External
options.body: Use the custom-provider/docs path and ask any maintained Atomic Chat provider package to live as a ClawHub/npm provider unless a missing core API is found.

options.title: Sponsor Bundled Provider
options.body: Accept Atomic Chat as first-party bundled surface, then require the implementation PR to resolve conflicts, dependency approval, labeler coverage, and review findings.

options.title: Defer Decision
options.body: Leave the issue and PRs open until maintainer demand or ownership evidence clarifies whether bundling is worth the support cost.

recommendation.title: Keep External
recommendation.body: Use the custom-provider/docs path and ask any maintained Atomic Chat provider package to live as a ClawHub/npm provider unless a missing core API is found.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across provider plugin architecture, self-hosted helper boundaries, and local-model docs that define the bundling decision.
